global-options.option: Properties file with cf.* settings, UTF-8.
Legacy fw.properties file to import below every cf.* source; repeatable, later files win; every key is reported with its disposition (revision 2, decision F6-F31).
Override one cf.* setting; repeatable; wins over the file and the environment.
Constraint sidecar to apply (params, orders, constraints; shortcut for --set cf.constraints.file=FILE); without it a scenario's companion <stem>.constraints.json is read.
Output format of the report on standard output; default text.
Print stack traces for unexpected failures.

command.name: run
command.summary: Execute a scenario end to end: validate, plan, generate, execute, analyze.
command.option: Scenario to run (XLSX, JSON, YAML or TOML).
Write the run report artifact to PATH; enables cf.artifacts.enabled.
Write quiescent checkpoints to PATH; enables cf.checkpoint.enabled and cf.artifacts.enabled.
What runs the candidates: generated-java or a SUT plugin id (shortcut for --set cf.execution.sut=ID).
The run's name in every sample key (shortcut for --set cf.run.id=ID).

Instead of a scenario, run the Java candidates of a legacy bundle.handoff/v2 hand-over (its manifest.json and loose source files); its run id and verdict mode apply unless set explicitly. Any other protocol version is refused.

command.name: validate
command.summary: Validate the configuration and, when one is given, a scenario, without running anything.
command.option: Scenario to validate as well (scenario validation arrives with M01).

command.name: plan
command.summary: Validate a scenario and print its plan: operators, exact cardinalities with formulas and row lengths, the candidate and sample counts with how sure each is (exact, bounded, estimated, unknown), resource estimates.
command.option: Scenario to plan.
The most candidates the exact counts may visit; default 1000000.
Also write the FW_Seq dependency graph as fwgen graph wrote it: Graphviz DOT when FILE ends in .dot, its JSON otherwise.

command.name: candidates
command.summary: Validate, plan, generate and assemble a scenario's candidates: counts (generated, excluded by rules, left out by covering selection, executable), per-rule impact and the first candidates with their ids and sources.
command.option: Scenario to assemble.
How many candidates to show, from the first; default 10, 0 for none.
The most candidates the exact counts may visit; default 1000000.
Also write every executable candidate as a legacy bundle.handoff/v2 hand-over into DIR, which must be new or empty: one file per candidate, or shards with --transport sharded.
How --export packs the candidates: loose-files (the default) or sharded.

command.name: analyze
command.summary: Analyze an exported results artifact: metrics, coverage, Pareto fronts, optimizers.
command.option: Results artifact to analyze.
Import existing coverage metrics; requires --coverage-report. Runs no coverage tool.

Coverage report path relative to the working directory; {lineNo} is the physical one-based results line. Requires --coverage-format. Imported metrics override inline keys; missing/malformed reports are diagnosed.

command.name: resume
command.summary: Resume a run from an explicit checkpoint artifact.
command.option: Checkpoint artifact to resume from.
Write the run report artifact to PATH.

command.name: export
command.summary: Convert a checkpoint artifact into a report, legacy results_v2 rows or a metrics table.
command.option: Checkpoint artifact to read (run --checkpoint PATH writes one).
File to write; replaced only once complete.

What to export: report (XML summary, the default), results (legacy results_v2 rows, one per attempt, CSV), csv (final samples with their metrics), html (the run as one self-contained page with its triage findings, the legacy bundle report) or metrics (the metrics corpus analyze --results reads: one key=value line per sample with its verdict as FW_VAR).

command.name: score
command.summary: Score the logical lines of a text file with the legacy analyzer's heuristic rules: a frozen corpus profile, named contributions and opt/watch/reject decisions. Runs nothing; decisions never make a sample eligible.
command.option: UTF-8 text to score; lines join into logical shell commands.
The legacy analyzer's manual rules (JSON: required/forbidden tokens, keys and regexes, token weights, expected types and signatures, line_length, numeric_ranges, optimizations).
Lines a common token, key or number needs; default 3.
Common tokens, keys and numbers kept; default 12.
Score from which a line is opt; default 75.
Score from which a line is watch; default 45.
Instead of scoring, suggest goals from the first 500 lines (the legacy Auto-Analysis plan): manual-rules JSON and a cf.analysis.goals value. Never enables execution.

command.name: desktop
command.summary: Open the Swing desktop: validate and plan a scenario, run, pause, resume and cancel it with its progress and report, analyze results and score texts. Needs a display; refused on a headless JVM.
command.option: Scenario to open.

command.name: guif
command.summary: Open the FlatLaf desktop with the shared Java workflows and the integrated Sieve constraint workbench. Needs a display; refused on a headless JVM.
command.option: Scenario to open.

command.name: decompose
command.summary: Split a source file into byte-preserving pieces and write the fwgen spec the legacy code_decompose.py wrote: one raw slot per piece with its original text, interaction notes from shared names; rewrites added to the slots are combined and reassemble into programs. Nothing is run.
command.option: Source file to split.

java splits the first type at the members the JDK parser finds; java-heuristic is the legacy scanner; generic splits at blank lines; py splits at the top-level statements as the legacy ast decomposition did; auto (default) picks py when the text parses as Python, else java or generic, as the legacy tool chose.
Logical name in the spec; default the file name without extensions.
Write the spec here and list the pieces; default standard output.
Split pieces longer than N characters at line ends (the spreadsheet cell holds 32767); default 0, off.

command.name: triage
command.summary: Turn a finished run's verdicts into findings: failures grouped by what distinguishes them, a minimal witness for each and the declared values that explain them, as the legacy bundle triage reported. Reads only what the run persisted; nothing is executed.
command.option: A checkpoint (run --checkpoint PATH writes one), a legacy run directory holding metrics.kv or executor-summary.json, or a directory with runs/RUN/ (the latest is read).
How many enrichment rows the text report shows; default 12.
Also write the legacy bundle.triage/v1 JSON report to FILE.
Also write triage.json into the run directory (beside a checkpoint).
Exit 1 (ANALYSIS_FINDINGS) after the report when the run has any finding.

command.name: doctor
command.summary: Probe this environment for the resolved configuration, read-only: the Java runtime, its compiler, memory budget against heap, the working directory, the SUT plugin and capability refusals, each OK, WARNING or BLOCKING as the legacy bundle doctor reported; exits 1 only when a check is blocking.
command.option: Scenario whose static Python imports are inspected from a bounded preview; no candidates or preprocessing run.
Also write the cf.doctor/v1 JSON report to FILE.

command.name: benchmark
command.summary: Time each stage on its own at a size profile, as the legacy bundle bench did: generator, sieve, executor and analyzer in this JVM, with the environment that makes the figures comparable (JDK, heap, hardware, workers, seed); no end-to-end or billion-execution throughput is claimed.
command.option: Candidates per stage; default 10K. Above 10,000,000 only with --allow-huge.
Comma-separated stages: generator, sieve, executor, analyzer; default all.
Allow a profile above 10,000,000 candidates.
Also write the versioned JSON report (cf.benchmark/v1) to FILE.

command.name: capabilities
command.summary: Print what this build implements, what is not built yet, and what is incompatible by design.

exit-codes.exit-code: The command completed. For run: the run reached COMPLETED.
The run reached FAILED, or the command failed unexpectedly (a framework defect).
The command line is invalid: unknown command or option, missing or malformed value.
Configuration, scenario or plan validation found errors; no run entered RUNNING.
The request needs a capability this build does not provide.
A configured budget stopped the work explicitly; nothing was dropped silently.
The process received an interrupt signal (SIGINT convention: 128 + 2).
